2610.05437.title: TeleTune: Evolving Agent Skills From Offline Telemetry
2610.05437.paper_summary: Computer-use agents need to capture procedural knowledge of how people use software. User telemetry offers a scalable source of this knowledge. However, learning reusable skills from these logs requires addressing three challenges: (1) Goal Underspecification, since logs do not record the goal behind each action; (2) Non-Replayability, since past activity cannot be replayed to evaluate skill updates; and (3) Interleaved Trajectories, since logs may mix several tasks without marking their boundaries. To address these, we introduce TeleTune, a framework for learning a textual skill library from offline logs without recorded goals, cannot be replayed during optimization, and may interleave tasks. TeleTune uses action-prediction errors on logged trajectories to propose library edits and keep only those that improve held-out action-prediction accuracy, which we call skill-guided progress. The learned workflows also enable retrieval of demonstrations that cover the subgoals of a new task. At test time, the agent is provided with the learned library and the workflow-based retrieved demonstrations. Experiments on WorkArena and Online-Mind2Web show that TeleTune outperforms random retrieval, Agent Workflow Memory (AWM), and their combination. We find that the best baseline varies by setting, whereas TeleTune achieves average success rates of 77.1% and 80.6%, respectively, improving over the strongest baseline on each benchmark by 6.7% and 7.7%. Under the heaviest perturbation of the WorkArena training data,TeleTune keeps the highest average success rate at 68.5%, 6.3% above the strongest baseline. Our analyses show (1) skill optimization and workflow-based retrieval are complementary, (2) optimizing on fixed logs costs 5 to 75 times fewer tokens than validating the same edits with live episodes, (3) skill-guided progress tracks the live success rate.
2610.05437.paper_summary_zh: 電腦使用代理需要捕捉人們使用軟體的程序性知識。用戶遙測提供了這種知識的可擴展來源。然而，從這些日誌中學習可重用的技能需要解決三個挑戰：(1) 目標未明確，因為日誌未記錄每個行動背後的目標；(2) 無法重播，因為過去的活動無法重播以評估技能更新；以及 (3) 交錯的軌跡，因為日誌可能混合了幾個任務而未標記其邊界。為了解決這些問題，我們介紹了 TeleTune，一個從離線日誌中學習文本技能庫的框架，這些日誌沒有記錄目標，無法在優化過程中重播，並且可能交錯任務。TeleTune 利用記錄的軌跡上的行動預測誤差來提出庫編輯，並僅保留那些能提高保留行動預測準確性的編輯，我們稱之為技能引導進展。學習到的工作流程還能檢索涵蓋新任務子目標的示範。在測試時，代理會獲得學習到的庫和基於工作流程的檢索示範。在 WorkArena 和 Online-Mind2Web 上的實驗顯示，TeleTune 超越了隨機檢索、代理工作流程記憶 (AWM) 及其組合。我們發現最佳基準因設置而異，而 TeleTune 分別達到 77.1% 和 80.6% 的平均成功率，分別比每個基準上最強基準提高了 6.7% 和 7.7%。在 WorkArena 訓練數據的最重擾動下，TeleTune 保持了最高的平均成功率 68.5%，比最強基準高出 6.3%。我們的分析顯示 (1) 技能優化和基於工作流程的檢索是互補的，(2) 在固定日誌上優化的成本比用實時集驗證相同編輯少 5 到 75 倍，(3) 技能引導進展跟踪實時成功率。
